title: De-labeling of beta-lactam antibiotic allergy in pediatrics through oral exposure to beta-lactam antibiotics (BLA)
summary:
This study focuses on the evaluation of a diagnostic risk score used to identify children who are at low risk of allergy to beta-lactam antibiotics (BLA), even though they have a suspected diagnosis of antibiotic allergy. Many people report in their medical history that they are allergic to these antibiotics, but in reality only a few are affected. Patients who are incorrectly classified as allergic often receive less suitable alternative medications, leading to poorer treatment outcomes and an increased risk of developing resistance.

The aim of the study is to lay the groundwork for strategies to review existing allergy diagnoses and correct them if necessary. The aim is to establish a standardized procedure that can be used in everyday clinical practice even after the study has been completed. Study participants are carefully selected to ensure that the risk of an actual allergy is low. Various pediatric risk scores are used and evaluated as part of the study. Oral provocation testing is performed as part of the usual diagnostic evaluation when antibiotic allergy is suspected. During this test, participants receive a small dose of a beta-lactam antibiotic under medical supervision. Participants are closely monitored so that immediate medical intervention can be provided in the event of a possible allergic reaction.  Over the following two days, the antibiotics are continued at home. This procedure complies with the current recommendations in Germany for diagnostic clarification in cases of suspected antibiotic allergy in children.
conditions: Personal history of allergy to drugs, medicaments and biological substances

interventions.name:
The participants receive a weight-adjusted single dose of the index BLA to be tested orally under clinical supervised conditions.
On days 2 and 3, administration of the BLA orally is continued at home.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Case history of BLA allergy.
- Pediatric risk assessment (adapted risk score) as low or very low risk for antibiotic allergy.
- Patient consent and/or parental consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who do not have a low or very low risk of antibiotic allergy and/or who have not given their consent to participate in the study.
